about: The Gate 2 board's own words and the drawings it shows. gate_2_board_build.py reads this file on every run; every figure it prints from other files is read at build time. Codes in a 'refs' field print only in the small reference line under a panel or card. Image specs: copy (a file to copy), svg (a file to draw, h in px), sprite (a fifth edition symbol from work/boards/sprite-sheet.html), element (a part of a page to photograph) or crop (a box of an image). The 'phase3' block is the main session's to fill.
title: Gate 2 Evidence Board

cover.title: The evidence for Gate 2
deck: Phase 2 refined the identity, drew the symbol families and built sixteen chapters of the guide. This board sets each refinement you approved beside the drawing it replaced, at the size a reader meets it, with the checks the studio ran on every mark.
A few panels wait on teammates who are still at work. Each says whose file it waits for, and fills in when that file lands.
cover.minutes: Each panel opens with its answer in a sentence or two. The detail sits below it for when you want to look closer.

pending_line: Waiting for {who}. This panel fills in when {file} lands.

approves.title: What you approve at Gate 2
approves.lede: Gate 1 named four choices for this gate. You answered three of them during Phase 2, so the plan for Phase 3 is the one still open.

answered.body: On November 7 you kept today’s width. The condensed drawing stays in the files as a record and leaves the proofs.
You approved it by name in the same answer. The next panel sets it beside the fifth edition’s ampersand at four sizes.
On November 8 Civic Line’s topic drawings became the topic set, and on November 9 you confirmed every Civic Line drawing as final. Testify, Contact an official and Housing joined the set after that.

approves.phase3_pending_file: the panel’s words from the Phase 3 proposal
approves.settled_lede: Gate 1 put three questions on Phase 3’s list. You answered each during Phase 2, so the proposal builds on your answers.

settled.body: A chart that splits from a midpoint runs from Prussian through the page color to Verdigris, with a boxed arrow for the direction.
Charts draw on our systems atlas and on primary public sources, each with a full source line. Any other data carries an Illustrative data label beside the chart.
Example bills in trackers stay invented, each labeled Illustrative beside it.

refinements.title: Each refinement beside what it replaced
refinements.lede: Every drawing here sits at its true size in pixels, as a 1x screen draws it, on the surface you approved it for. Where detail matters, a second view shows the same pixels at twice the size, so you can see where each edge lands.
refinements.source_note: The fifth edition’s drawings are the earlier boards’ proofs of it, made from its own files in October. Edition 06’s drawings come from the approved files the guide uses today.
refinements.key_zoom: Twice the size, pixel for pixel

craft.lede: Every icon drawn for 16 and 24 px passes the pixel-fit check on today’s files, and every symbol in the guide’s sprite draws the same pixels as its own file.

similarity.lede: Ampersand B still reads as an ampersand and matches no font installed here closely enough to pass for it. Among the icons, the closest pairs the script finds are listed with their scores, so you can judge them by eye.

weight.title: Page weight, a risk for Phases 3 to 5
weight.lede: The guide stays one file, and the host takes pages up to 16 MB. Today’s chapters weigh {frozen_mb} MB, and the engineer projects the finished guide at {projected_mb} MB against a {budget_mb} MB budget, so chapter 14’s 127 chart forms carry most of the risk.

groups.h: The hinge diagram and the badge
Red’s job, and marks on Prussian

items.title: Wordmark masters for small sizes
items.what: The fifth edition scaled one drawing down, so its letters blurred at 16 and 24 px. Edition 06 draws a master for each size, with stems and bars on whole pixels and the ampersand at full height.

items.title: Ampersand B, a drawing of our own
items.what: The fifth edition set its ampersand from Lora Bold, a free font anyone can type. Ampersand B is one pen path that crosses itself, with a beak serif and a tail whose foot rests on the baseline, and it has its own masters at 16 and 24 px.

items.title: Equal white on both sides of the ampersand
items.what: Spaced by the nearest ink, the fifth edition left 1.24 times as much white to the right of the ampersand as to its left. Edition 06 moves the ampersand 1.42 font units toward ACTION, so both gaps hold the same white, and the wordmark keeps its width.

items.title: Six symbols that cut off their own edges
items.what: Six of the fifth edition’s symbols lost ink at the edges of their boxes: the ampersand, the stacked lockup, the one-line tagline, both lines of the two-line tagline and the web address. Edition 06 exports each in a box that holds all its ink, with the outlines unchanged.

rows.label: The stacked lockup, display size
rows.note: A new stacked lockup has replaced this one since November 7.

items.title: Lockmark masters for small sizes
items.what: At 24 px the fifth edition’s lockmark drew only 5 percent of its ink solid, so its nodes went soft. Edition 06 draws masters at 16, 24 and 48 px with each node on whole pixels and a larger lever. The 24 and 48 px files were rebuilt on November 10, so each node and the lever is one outline.

items.title: One minimum size for every mark
items.what: The fifth edition’s minimum sizes disagreed with each other. Edition 06 sets one rule: no mark draws its capitals under 14 px on screen, no tagline inside a lockup sets under 13 px, and each lockup names the mark that takes its place below its minimum.

items.title: The horizontal lockup for print
items.what: Since November 8 the masthead has set the lockmark at 2.18 times the height of the capitals, while print kept the October drawing at 2.4. The print master now takes the masthead’s proportion, so the lockup prints as it shows on screen. Both are drawn here with 40 px capitals.
cols: October master, in print until November 11

items.title: The sign-off on social cards
items.what: A social card now signs off with the 48 px lockmark master drawn at exactly twice its size, 96 px, so the mark holds up in a feed. Covers, posters and the masthead keep 48 px. Each card here is 1200 by 630 px, its true size.

cells.empty: No 48 px card was drawn on Charcoal.

items.title: The hinge diagram, drawn again
items.what: The fifth edition drew the hinge’s arc as a dotted line, the line our systems atlas uses for a hypothesis. The new diagram sets the ampersand in a ring between OATH and ACTION, with two solid hairline arcs that run clockwise.

items.title: The hinge-circle badge
items.what: A new mark with no words: ampersand B inside the hinge diagram’s ring. It signs an end mark, a report’s back cover and events, and never serves as an avatar or a favicon. The fifth edition had no badge, so the left column shows the Phase 1 drawing it grew from.

items.title: One job for red, and White on Prussian
items.what: Rule 05.3 gives red one working job in each view and keeps it off Prussian. On Prussian the fifth edition’s red ampersand measures {red_on_prussian} to 1, so identity marks there now take White, at {white_on_prussian} to 1.

items.title: The four pillar marks
items.what: Gate 1 approved Direction A, a geometric solid, for Explain, Track, Connect and Act. On October 29 you replaced it with Civic Line’s four drawings, which the guide uses today, with pixel fits at 16 and 24 px for 1x screens.

cells.empty: Drawn only at 16 and 24 px before it was replaced.

items.title: Civic Line in place of the fifth edition’s topic symbols
items.what: The fifth edition drew twenty topic symbols as filled shapes. Civic Line, the line drawings you made and approved as final, now draws topics and the atlas in one hand: {n_civic} drawings, used at 48 px and up, and at 24 px for the {n_24} that read there. Five subjects share a name in both sets, and they stand side by side here.
items.v5_set_h: All twenty of the fifth edition’s topic symbols, at 48 px
items.set_link: Every Civic Line drawing in use sits on the 48 px sheet in the craft panel.

items.title: Housing
items.what: Housing is a new Civic Line drawing: an apartment block beside a pitched-roof house on one ground line, with red on one window of the block. It serves at 48 px and up and stays off the 24 px list for now.

cells.empty: The fifth edition drew Housing at 48 px and smaller.

items.title: Pixel fits for drawings at 24 px
items.what: At 24 px a drawing made on a 128-unit grid lands between pixels and blurs. Each of the {n_fits} Civic Line drawings on the 24 px list now has a fit drawn on the 24 px grid, which 1x screens draw, while 2x screens draw the master. Six are shown here, and the craft panel holds all {n_24}, the four pillar fits among them.
cols: The fit, in use on 1x screens

items.title: Pause and Filter at 16 px
items.what: Two utility icons were redrawn at 16 px: Pause with 5 px bars, and Filter with a 5 px spout whose outer edges sit on whole pixels. Every other 16 px file and every 24 px file stays as you approved it on November 10.

items.title: Rule 12.4 retires the hinge arcs
items.what: The guide allowed one pattern, arcs drawn from the hinge, in the open corner of a cover. On November 11 you retired it: an open area now stays plain, or carries the large crop of ampersand B or a watermark. Both covers are invented, and each is labeled Illustrative.

craft.pixel_h: The pixel-fit check, run on today’s files
craft.pixel_lede: A drawing passes at a size when it passes on a 1x and a 2x screen: its thinnest stroke covers at least one device pixel, every straight stroke lands within a tenth of a pixel of the grid, separate parts keep at least a pixel apart, and no counter fills in.
craft.housing_note: Housing, like every Civic Line master, is drawn on a 128-unit grid, so at 48 px its straight strokes fall between pixels. The check marks that as a miss on straight strokes, as it did on November 10, and its strokes, gaps and counters pass. The 48 px floor allows for it.
craft.sprite_lede: The guide draws its icons from one sprite. The check draws each symbol through the sprite beside its own file and compares every pixel.
craft.sprite_switch: {ok} of {n} drawings on the 24 px list draw their fit on 1x and 1.5x screens and their master on 2x screens, as the switch you approved asks.
craft.qa_lede: The October trace and its November successor, the set in use.

similarity.amp_h: Ampersand B against every serif ampersand installed here
similarity.amp_lede: Two tests, set before the run. B must overlap Lora Bold, the fifth edition’s source, by 0.70 or more, so a reader still knows it. It must overlap every other face by less than the median overlap of one family’s Regular and Bold, {calib}, so no installed font could pass for it.
similarity.amp_sheet_cap: The faces closest to B, each scaled to the same ink height, with its overlap. Overlap runs from 0, no shared ink, to 1, the same shape.
similarity.amp_not: Commercial faces are not installed here, so the check could not include them.
similarity.icons_lede: The script blurs each drawing’s ink at 24 px, compares shapes and ranks every score against the {pairs} pairs among the Civic Line masters. A score in the top 1 percent is flagged, and one in the top 5 percent is watched.
similarity.flagged_h: The flagged pairs, side by side at 24 px
similarity.flagged_lede: You approved all 37 fits with these pairs in view. Each pair stands here so you can judge it again.
